doc.title: Percy Humphrey Band: Percy Humphrey, Jim Robinson, Ernest Roubleau, Josiah Frazier Interview, 1972-02-29

title: Playing Germany and Europe in 1966-67: music as a universal language
summary: Jim tells of tours with the All-Star Band in 1966 and George Lewis in 1967, and audiences who understood the music without the language.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: You see, let me tell them this too. You see they speak about saying music is a universal language. My first time going overseas in 1966. We had a place they called Copenhagen, Munich, Germany. Because it was working out of Frankfurt, Germany. The first night we played, the first number you played, everybody sounds looking at you in Germany. You think they're not. They're taking that music. They couldn't understand our language. And I'm from the south down here. My way of speaking, where the kicks will come out when we get into these different restaurants and girls we serve. They don't understand my language. They don't understand them. But some of the places have an interpreter. But that bandstand, when we played, see how they played that first set, the house came down. Screaming and clapping. You see how that music can reach them? Now where the kicks come out, like I had them laughing by the Pop Foster. Now I've been different parts of Germany. I worked Dusseldorf. I worked Frankfurt. I worked Baden-Baden. I worked Berlin. I stood up there with the All-Star Band 66. Then I went back there in 67 with George Lewis and them group. And we didn't play Berlin. Then we played London, England in 66. But like I said, but in Germany, England people understood us good. And when I went to Copenhagen, the place they called, in Switzerland, they understand us. And then Sweden the same way. But in Germany, that's why we run into trouble with our language. But that music can reach them people. You see? Yeah, they understand that, man. Music reach them all over the world. In the world, yeah. That lingo is something.
